Name: O lagudi ma howo’o wo djaga-djaga’a – The guardian of the legundi fruits
Description: O lagudi ma howo’o wo djaga-djaga’a starts out as a story about an abandoned boy who is taken in by a mysterious woman. In the middle of the story, the narrative focus shifts to seven princesses, one of whom is courted by the legundi fruit guardian. I am not sure whether the legundi fruit guardian and the abandoned boy are supposed to be one and the same person.
Citation: Zielenbach, Maria. 2026. O lagudi ma howo’o wo djaga-djaga’a – The guardian of the legundi fruits In Half silver, half gold: Modole folk stories and a first sketch grammar. Berlin: Language Science Press

Name: O Bibiti – The bibiti fish
Description: O Bibiti is the story of a girl who catches a supernatural bibiti fish. After the fish has completed several magical tasks, the girl is courted by a man who leads her away from her home. There she is found by a king who marries her and she turns out to be a supernatural being herself.
Citation: Zielenbach, Maria. 2026. O Bibiti – The bibiti fish In Half silver, half gold: Modole folk stories and a first sketch grammar. Berlin: Language Science Press

Name: O Goda – The goda spirit
Description: In the story O Goda, a man tries to prevent his wife from being seized by the goda spirit. This spirit is an integral element of North Halmaheran traditional religion. The man fails in his endeavor, but he and his wife can eventually escape the goda spirit.
Citation: Zielenbach, Maria. 2026. O Goda – The goda spirit In Half silver, half gold: Modole folk stories and a first sketch grammar. Berlin: Language Science Press

Name: O Gogunane – The ants
Description: O Gogunane can be called a trickster story. Two women disguised as ants tease an elderly couple. After escaping in a flying palace, they proceed to fight of a number of unwelcome suitors to be eventually married by a prince.
Citation: Zielenbach, Maria. 2026. O Gogunane – The ants In Half silver, half gold: Modole folk stories and a first sketch grammar. Berlin: Language Science Press

Name: O lia’a de o dodoto – The older and the younger brother
Description: O lia’a de o dodoto is the story of two brothers. After a conflict with his sister-in- law, the younger brother leaves and is followed by his older brother. They meet again but the younger brother prefers to seek his luck elsewhere. The younger brother encounters an old woman and seven princesses, and manages to marry one of them. His older brother also meets the old woman and the princesses and seeks to marry one of them. In this way, the younger brother – who has become a king – and the older brother are re-united.
Citation: Zielenbach, Maria. 2026. O lia’a de o dodoto – The older and the younger brother In Half silver, half gold: Modole folk stories and a first sketch grammar. Berlin: Language Science Press

Name: O uho – The cuscus
Description: O Uho is about a princess who marries a man disguised as a cuscus. Their children are taken away by her envious sisters and raised by an eccentric and cannibalistic general and his wife. Having escaped them as well as an presumptuous king, they are finally reunited with their parents and their father turns out to be a king as well. O Uho shares with the story O Gogunane the motive of a human disguised as an animal. But in contrast to the ants in Text D, the cuscus is not a trickster.
Citation: Zielenbach, Maria. 2026. O uho – The cuscus In Half silver, half gold: Modole folk stories and a first sketch grammar. Berlin: Language Science Press

Name: O Biara – The biara plant
Description: In O Biara a mother leaves her children because her daughter has fed the mother’s biara plant to her brother. The children follow her since the son needs to be nursed by his mother. Finally, the mother cuts off one of her breasts and the children plant it. The breast grows into a magical tree that spouts all manner of clothes and jewelry – and finally the mother herself.
Citation: Zielenbach, Maria. 2026. O Biara – The biara plant In Half silver, half gold: Modole folk stories and a first sketch grammar. Berlin: Language Science Press

Name: Naga o njawa ja mididi jo puaha – Two people who fasted
Description: In the story Naga o njawa ja mididi jo puaha, two brothers come home from fasting in the mosque to learn that their mother has slaughtered their chicken against their previous order. They therefore leave their home but get separated. The younger brother loses his way and encounters an old woman who takes him in. The motive of the old woman is also found in Text A and Text E.
Citation: Zielenbach, Maria. 2026. Naga o njawa ja mididi jo puaha – Two people who fasted In Half silver, half gold: Modole folk stories and a first sketch grammar. Berlin: Language Science Press

Name: O Lolabi mi tadi-tadi’a – She is stabbed by a kris
Description: In the story O Lolabi mi tadi-tadi’a, a suitor accidentally kills the girl he came to court. Her family demands that he be killed as well but he asks to be buried with her and in this way revives her.
Citation: Zielenbach, Maria. 2026. O Lolabi mi tadi-tadi’a – She is stabbed by a kris In Half silver, half gold: Modole folk stories and a first sketch grammar. Berlin: Language Science Press

Name: Cumu cagulu – Riddles
Description: The text Cumu Cagulu is not separately numbered in the original story collection but is included in the previous Text I. In contrast to the other texts, this is not a narrative but a collection of eight riddles.
Citation: Zielenbach, Maria. 2026. Cumu cagulu – Riddles In Half silver, half gold: Modole folk stories and a first sketch grammar. Berlin: Language Science Press
